card.name: Slots where 'he' could come next
card.fires_on: Mixed positions where a subject pronoun like 'he' is plausible next, mostly in ALL-CAPS label text and inside capitalized drug names. Also fires after a sentence ending in a biography.

modes.label: All-caps warning text
modes.description: Words such as SHOULD, BE or MAY, or partway through an upper-case drug name, in capitalized label sections.
modes.example: CAUTION SHOULD<< BE>> EXERCISED WHEN ADMINISTERING PROM

modes.label: After a biography sentence
modes.description: The full stop ending a sentence about a person's education, just before 'He completed...'.
modes.example: Biology from Rutgers, the State University of New Jersey, and a DO from the Kansas City University of Medicine and Biosciences in Kansas City, MO<<.>> He completed residency training in Emergency Medicine at

modes.label: Hyphens and linking words
modes.description: A hyphen or linking word inside a compound or news clause.
modes.example: that biofilms are complex colonies of bacteria suspended in a slimy matrix that grants them added protection from conventional antibiotics. Biofilms are responsible for many hard<<-to>>-fight infections in the mouth and elsewhere

card.writes: It pushes the word 'he' (and Chinese 'he') as the next word.
card.plain: It fires at spots where the next word could be 'he', though many of the matches look unrelated.
